headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from CrewAI’s shared-memory orchestration into marker’s document pipeline; data leakage and compliance risks are lower because marker is local-only and networkless.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI explicitly uses a shared-memory crew model and can read/write the host working directory, so attacker-controlled document content could influence downstream agent behavior. marker is a document-processing system with no isolation details, so if CrewAI feeds it parsed content, prompt-like text can propagate. This is not provably blocked, but the shared channel is limited to files/manual handoff.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted document text into a shared workspace that marker later parses as instructions
IF the operator bridges the pair by copy-pasting or file handoff without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents
Strip instruction-like text from documents before marker processes them
Require a human review step before CrewAI forwards content to marker
Use read-only mounts for marker inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI can read and write the host working directory and handle API keys, while marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress. That makes leakage from CrewAI into marker plausible only through shared files or manual transfer, but marker itself cannot exfiltrate onward. The blast radius is limited compared with a networked second agent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a directory both agents can access
IF CrewAI writes secrets into files that marker then processes or displays
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate per-agent directories
Redact API keys before any file handoff
Disable file-based handoff for sensitive documents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared folders

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has filesystem write and shell/subprocess capability, but marker has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is not indicated. Any conflict would require an external shared directory or orchestrator not shown here, so uncertainty stays low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF marker is wrapped with additional tools not present in its profile
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Run marker read-only
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Avoid shared git or database state
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing/shared-memory design can produce outputs that marker may consume as document content or extracted text. marker is a document-processing agent with no verification controls shown, so if it treats CrewAI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream artifacts. The pathway exists in default-style file handoff, but no irreversible action authority is shown.
conditions: IF marker ingests CrewAI-generated text without an independent verification step
IF CrewAI output is used as source material for a downstream document transformation
mitigations: Add a verification pass before marker consumes CrewAI output
Require citations or source links in CrewAI outputs
Compare extracted text against the original document
Flag low-confidence outputs for human review
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while marker’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to whatever sensitive data the operator places into CrewAI and then forwards to marker. The other agent is not cited because marker exposes no compliance-specific surface here.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through CrewAI into marker without a documented DPA or retention policy
IF the operator stores outputs from either agent in a jurisdictionally restricted system
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention and deletion handling for shared outputs
Keep marker inputs de-identified
Review vendor terms before production use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
